legs.name: clippy
legs.extract: select(.reason == "compiler-message") | select(.message.level == "error" or .message.level == "warning") | {type: "clippy", level: .message.level, file: ([.message.spans[]? | select(.is_primary)][0].file_name // .message.spans[0]?.file_name // "unknown"), line: ([.message.spans[]? | select(.is_primary)][0].line_start // .message.spans[0]?.line_start // null), lint: (.message.code.code // "compile-error"), message: .message.message}

legs.name: blocking-call-in-native-bif
legs.note: Line numbers in the --json output are ZERO-INDEXED, while ast-grep's default human report style is one-indexed: a finding printed as line 212 by the human formatter appears as "line": 211 here. Do not chase a phantom off-by-one. Exit 0 = no findings; exit 1 = at least one blocking construct in a native BIF body. Never pipe this leg -- there is no pipefail, so a pipe would report the downstream tool's status instead of ast-grep's.

legs.name: estate-guard
legs.note: ESTATE ASSERTION, NOT THIS REPOSITORY'S. A red here names a SUBJECT repository and the seat who ruled its obligation, and that subject is usually not this repo -- this battery is only the clock. Take it to the named seat; do not delete this leg because it inconvenienced your landing. It asserts two things per listed row: that the repository carries refs/guards/shared-tree (the promise) and that the class-A guard is installed there as ruled (the mechanism). The population comes from docs/tracking/must-be-claimed.tsv, never from this repo. The trailing root runs the REVERSE arm (claimed but unlisted) -- without it, claim-without-listing then unclaim is a complete bypass of the witness, and it costs ~38s.
